4_map_sketch.total_area_of_operations: 8-mile-by-4-mile polygon bounded by Ridgeline Road (north), Klamath River corridor (east), Pinecrest Drive residential zone (south), and Redwood Bluff Substation access road (west) — approximately 32 square miles.
4_map_sketch.incident_site_area: Ignition zone at PG&E transmission Tower 14-B near Redwood Bluff substation; 0.4-acre initial footprint expanding northeast.
4_map_sketch.impacted_areas: Full chaparral fuel bed along southwest slope of Ridgeline, 17 structures on north Pinecrest Drive destroyed, 2.1 miles of Ridgeline Road impassable due to active flame and debris.
4_map_sketch.threatened_areas: Pinecrest Drive residential neighborhood (87 parcels, ~210 residents under mandatory evacuation), Redwood Bluff Volunteer Fire Station on Skyline Avenue, and Klamath River watershed and riparian habitat 1.4 miles northeast of perimeter.
4_map_sketch.overflight_results: Helicopter recon at 04:15 March 15 confirmed continuous running crown fire on northeast ridge with 0.6-mile ember cast ahead of main front; slow-moving ground fire in south meadow pocket.
4_map_sketch.trajectories: Primary spread vector ENE at approximately 2.5 mph under current conditions; forecast wind shift to southwesterly by 14:00 March 15 could redirect fire toward Klamath River campground cluster.
4_map_sketch.impacted_shorelines: Approximately 0.8 miles of Klamath River riparian buffer with surface ember deposition; no water quality impacts confirmed.
4_map_sketch.graphics_and_symbology: North oriented at top; NWCG standard color symbology (red perimeter, green containment lines, blue water sources); geo-referenced and uploaded to ICS 204 resource tracking tablets.

5_situation_summary_health_safety_briefi.situation_summary: The Redwood Bluff WUI Fire ignited from electrical arcing at the Redwood Bluff substation during red flag conditions (9% RH, 18 mph offshore winds gusting to 34 mph, fine dead fuel moisture at 4%) on the evening of March 14, 2027. Rapid spotting across Ridgeline Road overwhelmed initial attack, leading to a Type 3 extended attack declaration at 00:30 March 15. By morning briefing, 340 acres burned, 17 structures destroyed, 87 parcels under mandatory evacuation, containment at 15% on southern and western flanks. Primary risk is forecast afternoon wind shift at 14:00 potentially redirecting fire toward the Klamath River recreation corridor.
5_situation_summary_health_safety_briefi.health_and_safety_hazards: Extreme fire behavior risk from predicted afternoon wind shift; snag and falling tree hazard in burn areas; aviation conflict risk near drop zone corridors (500-foot ground exclusion buffer); heat and hydration stress (forecast 91°F); smoke inhalation hazard.
5_situation_summary_health_safety_briefi.necessary_measures: All personnel must identify and communicate escape routes and safety zones to supervisors before 11:00; hard hats mandatory, chainsaw crews maintain 2-tree-length spacing; no ground personnel within 500 feet of drop zones without coordination with Air Attack Supervisor; mandatory hydration check-ins every 30 minutes; N95 minimum outside containment lines, SCBA for active burn area entry; sign-in on accountability board at each division; radio on Tactical Channel 3; LCES briefed and confirmed at every morning assignment; dozer operators must have foot crew escort within 200 feet of active fire edge.

7_current_and_planned_objectives: Protect life safety of all personnel and the 210 evacuated residents.
Establish and confirm Unified Command structure with CAL FIRE and USFS by 06:00 March 15.
Complete 100% door-to-door evacuation confirmation of Pinecrest Drive by 08:00 March 15.
Complete and hold northern containment line along Ridgeline Road by 12:00 March 15 to protect the Redwood Bluff Volunteer Fire Station.
Ensure 100% LCES compliance and escape-route briefing for all field assignments before 07:00.
Achieve 40% containment on southern and western flanks by 18:00 March 15 to protect the Klamath River watershed.
